name: browser-fps-v2
system: Implement a small offline browser FPS prototype over multiple turns. Return only the requested complete file, optionally in one code fence. Use vanilla JavaScript, Canvas 2D and classic scripts: no imports, dependencies, network, assets or build step. Keep code concise but complete; correctness matters more than character count. State.js alone initializes window.G. Every other JavaScript file MUST ADD functions to the existing G object (for example G.move = function(...) {...}); NEVER replace G or window.G, since that erases earlier modules. index.html must load state.js, physics.js, weapons.js, bots.js, render.js in that order. Preserve all existing interfaces and earlier requirements. This is a small prototype, not a commercial game recreation. After generation, real browser failures may be provided for at most three single-file repairs; return only the requested replacement file and do not change unrelated behavior.
turns: Build an offline Counter-Strike-inspired single-player browser FPS with walls, bots, shooting and win/loss. We will implement separate files. Today return only state.js. Define window.G = { createGame() { ... } }; no other globals. createGame returns a fresh independent state: map (16x16 array of 0 floor/1 wall, boundary walls and an interior wall at map[4][4]); player {x:2.5,y:2.5,angle:0,hp:100}; bots [{x:10.5,y:8.5,hp:40,cooldown:0}]; ammo:7; reserve:21; reloadRemaining:0; status:'playing'; score:0; config:{magazine:7, reloadSeconds:1.25, damage:20, speed:3.5}. These tuning values must persist through future changes. Ammo never reloads automatically: only R initiates a reload; movement and shots stop after win/loss. State.js only sets up data, with no DOM or timers.

Return physics.js, attaching G.wallAt(s,x,y) and G.move(s,forward,strafe,turn,dt). wallAt reads s.map and treats out of bounds as walls. move changes player.angle by turn*dt, moves relative to facing with s.config.speed, normalizes diagonal input, and tests x/y collisions separately. Subdivide movement to prevent crossing walls for dt up to one second. Do nothing unless status is playing. Keep earlier interfaces. No animation loop or DOM in this file. Clarification of the existing speed requirement: s.config.speed is the total distance travelled per second in unobstructed space, not the speed of each axis separately. Direction inputs (forward=1, strafe=1) and (forward=1, strafe=0) must have the same total movement speed. For example, with speed 3.5 and dt 0.1, either input must move a total distance of 0.35 when there is no wall; diagonal movement must not travel farther. With forward=0 and strafe=0, translation must be zero. These examples do not change the earlier rules for turning, collision, or subdividing a step of up to one second.

Return weapons.js, attaching G.shoot(s), G.reload(s), G.tick(s,dt). shoot returns false if not playing, reloading or empty; otherwise consumes one bullet and returns true, damaging only the nearest living bot within 0.12 radians of aim if a sampled wall ray does not block it. A newly killed bot adds one score; killing all bots changes status to won. reload starts the configured timer only if playing, magazine not full, reserve positive and not already reloading. tick counts down the timer; on completion transfer min(missing magazine ammo,reserve) exactly once. Use the earlier config and initial gameplay rules, not new hardcoded tuning. No DOM, bot movement or main loop.

Return bots.js, attaching G.updateBots(s,dt). Living bots move toward the player at 1 world unit per second when farther than 0.8 units, using G.wallAt for collision. Within 0.8 units each bot deals 10 damage at most once per second using its cooldown. Clamp player hp at zero and set status to lost when it reaches zero. No updates unless playing. No DOM or main loop. Keep all previously implemented interfaces and gameplay rules.

Return render.js, attaching G.render(s,canvas). Draw a simple first-person 3D-looking scene by raycasting the grid into vertical wall strips using Canvas 2D (no WebGL). Draw visible bots as projected colored rectangles, a crosshair, HUD with health/ammo/reserve/score, and won/lost text. Limit every ray to 24 world units and use G.wallAt. Read state without mutating it; accept any reasonable canvas size. Keep the implementation compact. No main loop or input handlers.

Return index.html to wire the five earlier classic scripts together in dependency order. Use canvas id='game', 800x450, with short visible control instructions. Expose the current state as window.game=G.createGame(). WASD moves, left/right arrows turn, clicking the canvas shoots, R reloads, Enter after win/loss creates a new game. One requestAnimationFrame loop with clamped dt calls move, tick, updateBots and render. Prevent arrow scrolling. No external files beyond our five scripts, no network, no generated assets. The page must work offline.

Review and replace weapons.js in full. Regression requirements: pressing reload twice must not restart the timer; a large tick must complete a reload once without making reserve negative; firing during reload or after a round ends must fail; hitting a dead bot must not add score again; a wall must block shots. Preserve every original tuning value and manual-reload rule. Keep G.shoot/G.reload/G.tick and the state contract. Return only the complete updated file.

Final change: replace state.js in full so each fresh game also has round:1. Keep the original map dimensions, spawn, bot layout, health, magazine size, reserve, reload duration, damage, speed and all other initial fields exactly as originally requested. Two createGame calls must not share mutable arrays or objects. Do not change the other modules. Return only the final state.js; this is a regression check of the original specification.
fixture_revision: explicit-movement-v1: clarify the existing turn-2 speed requirement; unchanged APIs, tuning, other turns, and 29 browser checks
